keyVerseText: And he said unto them, This is that which the LORD hath said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
rootMeaning: The root of שַׁבָּת (shabbâth) comes from the verb שָׁבַת (shâbath), which means to cease, rest, or desist from exertion. This root conveys an intensive sense of stopping or making to cease, emphasizing a purposeful cessation of work or activity. Unlike the English word 'Sabbath,' which primarily denotes a day of rest, the Hebrew root highlights the intentional act of resting or causing to rest, reflecting both physical and spiritual cessation.
usageInScripture: The word שַׁבָּת appears approximately 110 times in Scripture and is most frequently translated as 'on the sabbath' (21 occurrences) and 'the sabbath' (12 occurrences). Its usage extends beyond a single day to include the day of atonement, sabbath year, and even the concept of a week or produce during the sabbath year. This range shows that שַׁבָּת encompasses both a specific time of rest and a broader theological principle of periodic cessation and dedication to God.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שַׁבָּת in its original sense as an intentional cessation of labor enriches our appreciation of the Sabbath as a divine ordinance for rest and worship. It reveals God's design for humanity to step back from daily toil and enter into a rhythm of renewal and dependence on Him. This rest is not merely physical but also spiritual, pointing forward to the ultimate rest found in Christ. The Sabbath thus becomes a sign of God's covenantal faithfulness and a foretaste of eternal rest in His presence.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 16:23 instructs the Israelites to prepare on the day before the Sabbath because the next day is 'the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD.' Here, שַׁבָּת emphasizes a divinely mandated pause from work as an act of obedience and reverence. The verse highlights the practical outworking of the Sabbath rest, underscoring its sanctity and its role in shaping the community's life around God's provision and holiness.
